title: Regular Morley tetrahedra from p-secting planes

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
Tran replaced the trisecting planes of the Morley construction for a tetrahedron by p-secting planes, with one parameter for each pair of opposite edges, and conjectured that a regular Morley tetrahedron forces a pair of opposite edges whose four cross edges are equal (arXiv:2609.06553, Conjecture 8.6). We show that every isosceles tetrahedron with three different edge lengths is a counterexample: its Morley tetrahedron is regular exactly when one vertex lies on one of four lines through the centre, and every such point occurs. When all three parameters equal 4, only the regular tetrahedron remains.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX source with the figures as PNG, arXiv tarball), the dated priority check, and independent checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4 with Mathlib, in which every statement of the paper is formalized without sorry and the disproof is the theorem Morley.tran_false.
